name: Familial Articular Hypermobility Syndrome

criteria.description: Arthralgia for longer than 3 months in four or more joints
Soft tissue rheumatism (e.g., >3 lesions such as epicondylitis, tenosynovitis)
Positive family history of familial articular hypermobility syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Two major criteria or one major and two minor criteria or four minor criteria
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical; genetic testing is not routinely diagnostic.

imaging: MRI or ultrasound showing joint subluxations or soft tissue abnormalities
Echocardiography for mitral valve prolapse assessment
genetic: No specific gene identified; familial inheritance pattern observed
other: Beighton score assessment for joint hypermobility
Clinical evaluation of joint instability and soft tissue involvement

distinguishingFeatures: More prominent skin hyperextensibility and fragility
Presence of systemic complications such as vascular fragility
Characteristic skeletal features (e.g., tall stature, arachnodactyly)
Aortic root dilation and lens dislocation

redFlags: Severe joint pain disproportionate to clinical findings
Signs of vascular fragility or spontaneous arterial rupture
Progressive neurological symptoms such as cervical myelopathy
references: Orphanet: Familial articular hypermobility syndrome - ORPHA:2295
Castori M, et al. Familial articular hypermobility syndrome: clinical features and diagnostic criteria. Am J Med Genet A. 2010.
Tinkle B, et al. Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome: Clinical description and natural history. Am J Med Genet C Semin Med Genet. 2017.
